record.paper_title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
record.original_question: How can the resilience of a social organization be controlled using network interventions? The question should include identifying driver nodes, choosing the type and amount of intervention, modeling how control signals affect agent utilities, and forecasting how resulting local decisions propagate through network topology and dynamics.

evidence.quote: Questions • How can we control resilience using network interventions?
They require to ﬁrst identify the driver nodes, i.e., those agents that should be targeted, and secondly to decide about the type and the amount of interventions
But the method requires a model of the organization to forecast the impact. Further, it assumes that the agent’s utility is known.
Changing agents’ utility has the advantage of inﬂuencing these decisions. If agents leave or reorganize their links, this changes the network topology and impacts the dynamics in each layer.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction concerning the control of resilience in social organizations via network interventions. There is related literature on network controllability (Liu–Slotine–Barabási) and on resilience of complex networks (Gao–Barzel–Barabási), but no general framework jointly addressing driver-node selection, utility-based agent decisions, and multilayer propagation for resilience control appears to have been established. The problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Controllability of complex networks
status_evidence.snippet: Liu, Slotine and Barabási develop a framework for identifying driver nodes in linear network control, but do not address utility-driven agent decisions or resilience.
status_evidence.claim: Driver-node control theory exists for linear dynamics but does not cover utility-based social resilience.

status_evidence.title: Universal resilience patterns in complex networks
status_evidence.snippet: Gao, Barzel and Barabási characterize resilience of networked systems via a one-dimensional reduction, without prescribing utility-based interventions.
status_evidence.claim: Resilience analysis exists but a control framework integrating utilities and multilayer dynamics is not provided.
